recent_posts.title: Tumbleweed Monthly Update - April 2026
recent_posts.summary: The first-ever openSUSE America Summit took place April 29 through May 1 in Barranquilla, Colombia, hosted at Universidad Libre with 321 attendees including developers, students, and IT professionals from across the globe. Topics covered ranged from cybersecurity (including a capture-the-flag competition), Linux migration, Netfilter/nftables, Kubernetes drift detection with ArgoCD, machine learning workflows, open-source data platforms, mesh networking for rural areas, and AI's impact on coding and packaging. Organized with support from SUSE, the Geeko Foundation, and local communities, the event sparked discussions about making the summit a recurring, traveling event across the Americas modeled after the openSUSE.Asia Summit.

recent_posts.title: Tumbleweed Monthly Update - April 2026
recent_posts.summary: openSUSE Tumbleweed's April 2026 monthly update covers a wide range of package updates and security fixes. Highlights include GNOME 50 and KDE Gear 26.04.0 as major desktop releases, GTK4 4.22 with a new native GtkSvg renderer dropping the librsvg dependency, Linux kernel advancing to 7.0.2, Mesa 26.0.4/26.0.5 with raytracing fixes, and LibreOffice 26.2. Developer-facing updates include PHP 8.5.5, SQLite 3.53.0, iproute2 7.0, and nano 9.0. Security received heavy attention with dozens of CVE fixes across WebKitGTK, CUPS, Python, Flatpak, sudo, OpenEXR, libxml2, libarchive, mozilla-nss, and more. The Copy Fail vulnerability affecting openSUSE flavors was also addressed.

recent_posts.title: openSUSE Asia Summit 2026 Call for Speakers
recent_posts.summary: The openSUSE Asia Summit 2026 Call for Speakers is now open. The event will be held on October 3–4, 2026, at Universitas Gadjah Mada in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Speakers from all backgrounds are invited to submit proposals on topics including openSUSE distributions, desktop environments, cloud/containers, security, IoT, and FOSS culture. Proposals must be 130–250 words in English, submitted by July 1, 2026, with speaker notifications on July 21. Travel support is available via the openSUSE Travel Support Program. In-person attendance is required; remote presentations are not accepted.

recent_posts.title: Quantum-Resilient Cryptography in the openSUSE Ecosystem
recent_posts.summary: libzupt, a new post-quantum cryptography SDK, has been officially released as a package in the openSUSE ecosystem (Leap and Tumbleweed). The library implements a hybrid ML-KEM-768 + X25519 approach for file and in-memory encryption, standardized by NIST in August 2024. It currently supports C++, Python, and Java (Node.js in development), aiming to make post-quantum cryptographic mechanisms accessible to developers. The library originates from the Zupt backup/compression project and is designed to help applications remain secure against future quantum computing threats such as Shor's Algorithm.

recent_posts.title: Following Up on ARMv9 Build Infrastructure
recent_posts.summary: openSUSE's Open Build Service (OBS) has been running NVIDIA Grace Hopper hardware since last June, enabling native ARMv9 builds for Tumbleweed packages. The infrastructure now handles complex workloads including the Linux kernel, LLVM, GCC, Python, and Qt frameworks with good success rates. Native builds on actual silicon eliminate risks from emulated cross-compilation such as ABI mismatches and instruction scheduling errors. The post also makes a broader case for hardware vendors to donate or lend machines to OBS, framing it as a continuous automated QA benefit for vendors whose products run Linux.

Other topics covered: the Claude Code npm source map leak exposing 512,000 lines of TypeScript and its supply chain security implications, syslog-ng benchmarks reaching 7 million events per second, KDE Plasma 6.6 accessibility improvements, Thunderbird Linux system tray progress, and KDE Plasma 6.7 development updates.

recent_posts.title: Tumbleweed Monthly Update - March 2026
recent_posts.summary: openSUSE Tumbleweed's March 2026 monthly update covers a wide range of package updates and security fixes. Highlights include three KDE Plasma 6.6 point releases with progressive bugfixes to KWin, Spectacle, and Kicker; KDE Frameworks 6.24.0 with nanosecond-precision timestamps in KIO; Linux kernel progression from 6.19.5 to 6.19.9 with broad hardware and filesystem fixes; Mesa 26.0.2 resolving RDNA 4 visual corruption and a Counter-Strike 2 regression on Intel Arc; and GStreamer 1.28.1 adding speech-to-text transcription and AV1 decoding. Security was a major theme, with dozens of CVEs addressed across FreeRDP, curl, libsoup2, the kernel (ksmbd), Python, bind, ImageMagick, GraphicsMagick, exiv2, QEMU, and many more packages. libxml2 2.15.2 dropped its built-in HTTP client and aligned HTML serialization with HTML5.
